newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU commission opposed to French GAN bidder - paper.
newsitem.headline: EU commission opposed to French GAN bidder - paper.

text.p: The European Commission is opposed to a French company bidding for insurer GAN when the 80-percent state-owned group is privatised, the Liberation daily said.
The paper said this was mentioned in internal documents of the DG IV competition directorate of the European Union's executive commission.
It means Brussels would oppose a bid by AGF.
The paper quoted the document as including a reference to AGF as "the only likely French candidate."

"(AGF) is still financially fragile. It seems difficult for the AGF to finance with its own means an acquisition of GAN," the paper quoted the document. It added AGF could finance the deal by a capital increase to which the French state, which has seven percent since privatisation, would have to subscribe.

The note said that a link between GAN and AGF "would reduce the distance with the leading group AXA-UAP and other competitors, but would increase the concentration of the market" which would lead to "a reduction of the level of competition in France".

In Brussels, European Union sources denied the Liberation article, saying the EU's decision on Wednesday to approve 23 billion francs in state aid says GAN should be sold to a "strong" company capable of ensuring GAN's long-term viability.
The Commission tied its approval of the state rescue plan to a sell-off of GAN, France's fifth largest insurer, and its CIC CICF.PA banking subsidiary.

Under the terms of the bail-out, the second in two years, the state will inject 11 billion francs to cover property losses at GAN's UIC unit, and 9.9 billion in guarantees for future losses in restructuring the GAN group.
The government also injected 2.86 billion francs into GAN in 1995, bringing total state help of 23.76 billion francs.
